experiment: Does OCR hard-wrapping cause Station-3 grounding losses?
why: Page OCR hard-wraps prose every ~23 chars (44 newlines per 1k). A model quoting a span across a wrap renders it with a space, so exact char alignment fails and the extraction is DISCARDED by the grounding gate. Settled before the key-gated station-2 embedding commits the chunk store to a shape.

setup.chunks: same slice, page >= 60 (front matter excluded), station-0 verbatim store
arms: unwrapped (--unwrap: rejoins wrapped prose, preserves columnar/math lines)

unwrapped.note: run died on an Ollama 120s timeout at chunk 23; raw counts unavailable, so rate-of-raw is not comparable. Per-chunk yield and exact/fuzzy mix are.

finding: Unwrapping does NOT change how much is extracted (1.60 vs 1.59 grounded per chunk) but substantially improves how precisely it aligns: exact-match share 45% -> 69%. Fuzzy matching is our own whitespace-tolerant fallback; exact alignment is what gives trustworthy character-level provenance.
recommendation: Unwrap prose at station 0 before embedding. Yield is unaffected, citation precision improves, and doing it pre-embedding avoids paying the key-gated embedding cost twice.
limits: Small sample (25 vs 22 chunks; 40 vs 35 rows), one small model, one book. Directionally consistent with the mechanism but not statistically strong. The 16.5% vs the old 54.1% summary-chunk rate is NOT a regression: summary prose was clean LLM-written English that is trivially quotable, and those citations pointed at a paraphrase rather than the book.
harness_bug_fixed: The crash discarded the whole run's report despite 22 chunks of completed work. Per-chunk model failures are now caught and counted (chunk_errors), and report.json is written in a finally block with a `complete` flag.
